headline: Executive order signed in May 2022 sets federal policing and criminal justice policies aimed at accountability, public trust, and public safety.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order directs the federal government to change how policing and criminal justice work, with a focus on making law enforcement more accountable and effective. It aims to build public trust while keeping communities safe. No official summary was provided, so the specific rules, deadlines, and programs are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal law enforcement agencies and officers
who_it_affects.how: They are likely the main group directed to follow new or updated policing practices and accountability rules.

who_it_affects.group: People who interact with police or the criminal justice system
who_it_affects.how: They may be affected by changes in how officers and agencies are expected to act and be held accountable.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 25, 2022; executive orders usually take effect when signed, though specific parts may have later deadlines.
